description: The named target for tests/run.py --target. kind command: a server the harness starts in its own process group ({port} and {inspector_port} are free ports, never 8790; {dir} is the target's folder; {log_dir} the run's result folder; an argument "{wrangler}" is the repository's pinned wrangler, npm exec --no -- wrangler, or FEMTO_WRANGLER) and stops with every child; dir: the folder it serves, which <name>:<path> replaces (dist:<path> serves any built folder exactly like dist); requires: a path that must exist first ({dir} filled in); env: environment variables for the command ({port}, {dir} and {log_dir} filled in). ready: the readiness hook run before a check (static, none). See tests/README.md.

dist.about: The static site: wrangler pages dev dist (or dist:<path>, any built folder), with the wrangler pinned in package.json.
dist.env_why: wrangler writes a debug log on every run; WRANGLER_LOG_PATH keeps it in the run's result folder instead of ~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/logs.
dist.dir_why: dist:<path> serves another built folder (a relative path is read from the repository root) exactly like dist: the same wrangler, options and readiness, so several agents can each test their own build at once.
dist.command_why: {wrangler} is npm exec --no -- wrangler, the wrangler pinned in package.json (--no never downloads one; targets.py checks node_modules/wrangler against the exact pin first). --persist-to gives each server its own state folder in the run's folder, so concurrent servers never share .wrangler/state.
